parts: Please read the manuscript in /papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy. Can you describe the results so far at a high level, and what are the remaining obstacles? Please use equations and cite the manuscript where appropriate.
I’ll read the manuscript and its status notes, then trace the main results and remaining obstacles to the relevant equations and sections.

The manuscript certifies that the 24-site approximation slightly overestimates the squared gap throughout one time interval. The two zeros there were already known to be real. The open question is whether a finite Jacobi calculation can recover that correction using less information from the full theta field.

**The 24-site Jacobi approximation places one known pair of Newman zeros slightly too far apart throughout \(0\le t\le 10^{-4}\).** Inside the circle \(\Gamma=\{|z-36|=9\}\), both the complete theta field \(F\) and its approximation \(G_{24}\) have one simple real zero in \((28,29)\) and another in \((42,43)\). Writing \(D=((z_+-z_-)/2)^2\) for the squared half-gap, the tightest certified enclosure is
\[
-4.957996104
<10^8\bigl(D_F(t)-D_{24}(t)\bigr)
<-4.957019318 .
\]
The initial zero count was already known. What the manuscript adds is the sign and size of the approximation error over the **whole time interval**. Its signed contour calculation resolves that sign, and direct root displacement using the same full-source data gives the narrower interval displayed above. [Manuscript PDF](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/output/pdf/jacobi-integer-hierarchy/jacobi_integer_hierarchy.pdf) · [§8, Table 1](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/evidence.tex:19)

## How the approximation reaches the zeros

**At fixed degree, the first omitted Jacobi link accounts exactly for the error in the heat equation.** The finite field \(G_N=(e^{izJ_N})_{00}\) is an \(N\)-node Gaussian quadrature for the Fourier transform of the theta measure. If \(\beta_j\) are the squared Jacobi links, its heat-equation error is
\[
R_N=(\partial_t+\partial_z^2+\beta_1)G_N
=\beta_N\beta_{N-1}\,\partial_{\beta_{N-1}}G_N .
\]
For a pair centered at \(c_N\), this gives
\[
\dot D_N
=2-4D_NM_N
-\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_\Gamma (z-c_N)\frac{R_N}{G_N}\,dz .
\]
Here \(2\) comes from the two zeros acting on one another, and \(M_N\) sums the influence of all the other zeros. The complete field has \(R_F=0\), giving the inherited law \(\dot D_F=2-4D_FM_F\). The manuscript follows the extra term through every integer exterior moment, accounting for both the changing field and the moving pair. In symmetric coordinates the equations remain regular at a collision, \(D=0\). They still form an infinite hierarchy: the equation for \(M\) already involves two higher moments. [§2, Eqs. (2.4)–(2.6)](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/source.tex:29) · [§3, pair law](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/hierarchy.tex:85) · [Eq. (3.17), lowest moment equations](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/hierarchy.tex:301)

**At fixed time, adding two sites gives an exactly computable field change \(G_{N+2}-G_N\).** To turn a field change into a gap change, suppose \(Y\) and \(Z\) each have two zeros inside the same circle, with a common buffer from its boundary. For small relative error \(q=(Z-Y)/Y\), the manuscript proves
\[
D_Z-D_Y
=-\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_\Gamma (z-c_Y)q(z)\,dz
+O\!\left(\|q\|_\Gamma^2\right).
\]
The first term preserves cancellation around the circle. Theorem 5.1 gives an explicit bound for the remainder, including the displacement of the pair center. On the certified degree-24 example, that nonlinear allowance is below \(2.85\times10^{-12}\). [Theorem 4.1](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/degree.tex:13) · [Theorem 5.1](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/signed.tex:10) · [§8, certified allowance](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/evidence.tex:15)

## Remaining obstacles

1. **Recover the sign with less information from the complete field.** The proposed \(24\to26\) step supplies \(q_0=(G_{26}-G_{24})/G_{24}\). The missing part is exactly
   \[
   q-q_0=\frac{F-G_{26}}{G_{24}}.
   \]
   This tail needs an independent bound over the circle and time interval, together with a bound on the complete relative error on the surrounding collar. If the finite signed integral retains the observed margin, a relative tail appreciably below \(3.2\times10^{-10}\) would suffice. The actual margin for the finite step remains to be established. [Eq. (5.5)](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/signed.tex:43) · [§9, source information](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/challenges.tex:2)

2. **Find a degree-by-degree argument specific to theta.** Theorem 6.2 constructs a continuous, even, compactly supported positive density for which \(D_{N+2}-D_N\) takes both signs infinitely often along the even degrees and along the odd degrees. Thus positivity and symmetry alone cannot ensure eventual monotonicity. One possible route is to show that the negative part \(\max(0,-D_N)\) tends to zero for the theta source, while identifying the same pair and proving \(D_N\to D_F\). Even that would yield \(D_F\ge0\); excluding a double zero requires a strictly positive margin. [Theorem 6.2](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/parity.tex:121) · [§9, degree iteration](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/challenges.tex:5)

3. **Carry the estimate to new times or heights.** Backward continuation needs a verified two-zero count, a positive starting gap, and control of the worst cumulative loss before any possible collision. That loss is weighted by the actual exterior moment through \(W(u,v)=\exp(-4\int_u^v M(s)\,ds)\). An endpoint improvement can coexist with a larger loss in the interior. The present certificate therefore leaves open new zero coverage and any stronger bound for the de Bruijn–Newman constant. [Theorem 4.3, weighted transport](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/degree.tex:259) · [§9, time transport](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/challenges.tex:14)

The project records the certificate under its [result summaries](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/result-summaries/README.md) in the [Jacobi entry](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/result-summaries/18_tensor_approximation_and_coefficient_bounds.md:709), and the scope of the comparison under [patterns to avoid](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/avoid/README.md) in the [matched-input comparison note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/avoid/11_certifying_the_known_and_tests_that_cannot_fail.md:130).

I think there might be an issue with the research overview and plan, because focusing on the 24-site Jacobi approximation sounds more like a numerical test more than an overall analytical framework or result. What is the larger strategy?
I’ll compare the original overview and plan with the current continuation note to see what role the 24-site calculation was meant to play and what analytical result the project is aiming for.

The plan records a deliberate choice. It pursued a bound for one isolated pair because the proposed induction lacked a theta-specific inequality. That explains why degree 24 entered the work and why success on that pair leaves the induction open.

**The larger strategy is to use the Jacobi coefficients of the theta source to prove how far a pair of its Fourier zeros can be followed backward in Newman time without colliding.** The degree \(N\) controls how much of the source is retained. The analytical question is whether adding coefficients gives a signed estimate for the *true* gap that remains useful as \(N\) increases. My previous answer gave the degree-24 certificate too much prominence. The original overview puts this joint degree-and-time question first. [Research overview, §1](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/research-overview/01_AGC_JH_RESEARCH_OVERVIEW_20261119.md:23)

**Why the hierarchy matters.** For a pair \(z_-,z_+\), let \(D=(z_+-z_-)^2/4\). Its motion in the complete field satisfies
\[
\dot D=2-4DM,\qquad
M=\sum_{\rho\ \mathrm{outside\ the\ pair}}
\frac{1}{(\rho-z_+)(\rho-z_-)}.
\]
The \(2\) is the mutual interaction of the pair. The rest of the zero set enters through \(M\), whose own evolution involves higher exterior moments. Suppose the pair is known to be real and separated at time \(t_*\). To carry it backward by \(U\), one needs an independent upper bound on its largest cumulative gap loss,
\[
\sup_{0\le v\le U}\int_0^v (2-4DM)(t_*-s)\,ds < D(t_*),
\]
while the contour continues to isolate the same pair. This gives the hierarchy a concrete job. It must control the combination of moments that can exhaust the starting gap. [Overview, §3](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/research-overview/01_AGC_JH_RESEARCH_OVERVIEW_20261119.md:129) · [Parent manuscript, cumulative continuation margin](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/manuscript/sections/04_continuation.tex:21)

**What the manuscript contributes analytically.** At fixed time, finitely many Jacobi coefficients determine \(G_{N+2}-G_N\) exactly. At fixed degree, the first omitted link determines the extra forcing caused by truncation. The manuscript connects these facts. Write \(\Delta\) for the change from \(N\) to \(N+2\), and \(r_N\) for the truncation force in the gap equation. Then
\[
(\Delta D)' +4M_N\Delta D
=\Delta r-4D_{N+2}\Delta M.
\]
This identifies exactly what a source estimate must control. Changing degree alters both the truncation force and the influence of the exterior zeros. Bounding their **signed combination** preserves cancellation that separate absolute bounds can lose. Theorem 4.3 integrates this identity on every subinterval. Theorem 5.1 turns a signed contour estimate into a gap estimate with an explicit quadratic remainder, even when the enclosed zeros meet. These results apply at general degree under the stated contour hypotheses. [Theorem 4.1](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/degree.tex:13) · [Theorem 4.3](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/degree.tex:259) · [Theorem 5.1](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/signed.tex:10)

**Where the plan narrows.** The plan sets out two possible outcomes. One is to start with a positive gap and prove that the accumulated degree and time errors leave a positive margin. The other is to allow a finite approximation to have a nonreal pair and prove that its negative part \(u_N=\max(0,-D_N)\) contracts as the degree increases. A proposed inequality is
\[
u_{N+2}\le(1-\alpha_N)u_N+\varepsilon_N,\qquad
\sum_N\alpha_N=\infty,\qquad \varepsilon_N=o(\alpha_N),
\]
with \(0<\alpha_N\le1\) on one parity. If the same pair is tracked and \(D_N\to D_F\), this would give \(D_F\ge0\). The missing theorem is a derivation of those gains and errors from the actual theta source. The manuscript proves that an even, positive, compactly supported density can have gap increments of both signs infinitely often on each parity. A general appeal to positivity cannot supply the induction. [Plan, §5](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/research-plan/01_AGC_JH_RESEARCH_PLAN_20261119.md:154) · [Theorem 6.2](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/parity.tex:121) · [Manuscript, §9](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy/manuscript/sections/challenges.tex:5)

Your concern is sharpest at degree 24. **On that example \(u_{24}=0\), so the proposed contraction factor drops out of the inequality altogether.** The certificate rigorously measures the bias between two already-real pairs. The planned \(24\to26\) calculation asks whether that bias can be predicted with less complete-source information. Even a successful answer would establish one step. The gap in the current plan is the passage from that step to a theta-specific estimate over a stated range of degrees and times. I would make that estimate the headline milestone and use the degree-24 case to test its constants.
